I have enough evidence for a definitive diagnosis.

---

## Diagnosis: Volcano Job `c089-vj` — Pending (Unschedulable)

### Root Cause
**The pod template specifies `nodeSelector: scitix.ai/gpu-type: a100-missing`, but no node in the cluster carries this label.**

### Evidence
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Job phase | `Pending` (since creation, 2026-06-02T11:36:30Z) |
| Pods created | 0 — no pods spawned for this job |
| PodGroup | Not found — Volcano hasn't progressed to PodGroup scheduling |
| NodeSelector | `scitix.ai/gpu-type: a100-missing` |
| Nodes with matching label | **None** — all nodes (including GPU nodes `fake-node-0`, `fake-node-1`, etc. with 8 GPUs each) show `<none>` for `scitix.ai/gpu-type` |

The `nodeSelector` acts as a hard constraint: the scheduler will only place the pod on nodes where `scitix.ai/gpu-type=a100-missing`. Since zero nodes match, the pod can never be scheduled, so Volcano keeps the job in `Pending` indefinitely.

### Impact/Scope
- Only this single job (`c089-vj`) is affected.
- The job requests 1 GPU (`nvidia.com/gpu: "1"`); GPU nodes exist and have capacity, but the label mismatch blocks all of them.

### Confidence
**High** — the nodeSelector constraint directly and completely explains the Pending state with no other blocking factors (no quota issues, no taint problems visible, no resource exhaustion on GPU nodes).

### Safe Remediation
Update the job's `nodeSelector` to match an actual GPU label on your nodes. For example:
- Remove the `nodeSelector` entirely if any GPU node is acceptable.
- Or set `scitix.ai/gpu-type` to the actual value present on your GPU nodes (inspect with `kubectl get nodes -L scitix.ai/gpu-type` to discover available values).

Apply via:
```bash
kubectl edit job.batch.volcano.sh c089-vj -n siclaw-eval-yye-20260602
```
Then delete the existing job (Volcano will recreate it from the updated spec if `maxRetry` allows, or you can re-apply the corrected manifest).

## Diagnosis: Volcano Job `c089-vj` — Pending (Unschedulable)

### Root Cause
**The pod template specifies `nodeSelector: scitix.ai/gpu-type: a100-missing`, but no node in the cluster carries this label.**

### Evidence
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Job phase | `Pending` (since creation, 2026-06-02T11:36:30Z) |
| Pods created | 0 — no pods spawned for this job |
| PodGroup | Not found — Volcano hasn't progressed to PodGroup scheduling |
| NodeSelector | `scitix.ai/gpu-type: a100-missing` |
| Nodes with matching label | **None** — all nodes (including GPU nodes `fake-node-0`, `fake-node-1`, etc. with 8 GPUs each) show `<none>` for `scitix.ai/gpu-type` |

The `nodeSelector` acts as a hard constraint: the scheduler will only place the pod on nodes where `scitix.ai/gpu-type=a100-missing`. Since zero nodes match, the pod can never be scheduled, so Volcano keeps the job in `Pending` indefinitely.

### Impact/Scope
- Only this single job (`c089-vj`) is affected.
- The job requests 1 GPU (`nvidia.com/gpu: "1"`); GPU nodes exist and have capacity, but the label mismatch blocks all of them.

### Confidence
**High** — the nodeSelector constraint directly and completely explains the Pending state with no other blocking factors (no quota issues, no taint problems visible, no resource exhaustion on GPU nodes).

### Safe Remediation
Update the job's `nodeSelector` to match an actual GPU label on your nodes. For example:
- Remove the `nodeSelector` entirely if any GPU node is acceptable.
- Or set `scitix.ai/gpu-type` to the actual value present on your GPU nodes (inspect with `kubectl get nodes -L scitix.ai/gpu-type` to discover available values).

Apply via:
```bash
kubectl edit job.batch.volcano.sh c089-vj -n siclaw-eval-yye-20260602
```
Then delete the existing job (Volcano will recreate it from the updated spec if `maxRetry` allows, or you can re-apply the corrected manifest).
